title: Level 01
theoryHtml:
Anatomy is a structure of human body,it’s included body shape Size & Parts. For example : heart , lungs, bones & Muscles.

Physiology is a function of Human body. For example : Heart (Cardiovascular system(Pumps blood)), Kidney(Urinary system(Remove the wastage)),Brain (Nervous system(control the body)), Lungs(respiratory system(exchanges the gases)), Stomach (Digestive system (Breakdown of food for absorption)).
notice: Study the theory, go to the task page, answer the questions, complete the level, and open the page for the next level.

mcqs.q: What is the primary scientific focus of Anatomy?
options: The physical structure, shape, and parts of the body

mcqs.q: Which of the following is considered an anatomical structure?
What is the primary function of Physiology?
options: Studying the operational function of the human body and its organs

mcqs.q: Which organ system is primarily responsible for pumping blood throughout the body?
What is the primary physiological function of the kidneys?
options: Remove wastage from the body through the urinary system

title: Level 02
theoryHtml:
Skeletal System provides the internal framework of the human body, consisting of 206 bones in adults. For example : femur , skull, ribs & vertebrae.

Bone Functions include structural support, organ protection, and mineral storage. For example : Cranium (Protects the delicate brain), Rib cage (Shields heart and lungs), Red Bone Marrow (Hematopoiesis(Produces red blood cells)), Long bones (Calcium reservoir(Stores calcium and phosphorus)).
notice: Study the theory, go to the task page, answer the questions, complete the level, and open the page for the next level.

mcqs.q: How many bones make up the adult human skeleton?
Which part of the skeletal system protects the brain?
What is the medical term for the production of blood cells in bone marrow?
What vital organs are protected by the rib cage?
Which mineral is predominantly stored inside bone tissue?

title: Level 03
theoryHtml:
Muscular System contains over 600 muscles that create movement, maintain posture, and produce body heat. For example : biceps , triceps, diaphragm & deltoid.

Three Muscle Types operate in human physiology. For example : Skeletal Muscle (Voluntary movement(Attaches to bones for locomotion)), Smooth Muscle (Involuntary control(Lines blood vessels and hollow GI organs)), Cardiac Muscle (Involuntary rhythmic beats(Pumps the myocardium of heart)).
notice: Study the theory, go to the task page, answer the questions, complete the level, and open the page for the next level.

mcqs.q: Which muscle type is under voluntary conscious control?
Where is smooth muscle primarily found in the human body?
options: In the walls of hollow internal organs and blood vessels

mcqs.q: What is a major physiological function of muscular contraction besides motion?
Which muscle is found exclusively in the human heart?
What connective tissue anchors skeletal muscles to bones?

title: Level 04
theoryHtml:
Cardiovascular System delivers oxygen, nutrients, and hormones to cells while carrying away carbon dioxide and metabolic waste. For example : arteries , veins, capillaries & heart chambers.

Circulation Dynamics depend on pressurized blood flow. For example : Left Ventricle (Systemic pump(Drives oxygenated blood through aorta)), Pulmonary Artery (Deoxygenated transport(Carries blood to lungs)), Capillaries (Microcirculation(Gas and nutrient diffusion across thin walls)).
notice: Study the theory, go to the task page, answer the questions, complete the level, and open the page for the next level.

mcqs.q: Which chamber of the heart pumps oxygen-rich blood into the aorta for systemic circulation?
What is the primary role of capillaries in human circulation?
options: Gas, nutrient, and waste exchange between blood and tissues

mcqs.q: Which blood vessels typically carry deoxygenated blood toward the heart?
What is the unique characteristic of the pulmonary veins?
options: They carry deoxygenated blood from the brain
They carry oxygenated blood from the lungs into the left atrium
They have thick muscular valves only
They connect directly to the liver

mcqs.q: How many chambers are there in the human heart?

title: Level 05
theoryHtml:
Respiratory System facilitates external respiration by taking in oxygen and expelling carbon dioxide. For example : trachea , bronchi, bronchioles & alveoli.

Pulmonary Mechanics coordinate pressure gradients in the thorax. For example : Diaphragm (Primary muscle(Flattens downward during inspiration)), Alveoli (Gas exchange site(Microscopic air sacs wrapped with capillaries)), Epiglottis (Airway valve(Prevents food aspiration into larynx)).
notice: Study the theory, go to the task page, answer the questions, complete the level, and open the page for the next level.

mcqs.q: Where does oxygen and carbon dioxide gas exchange take place in the lungs?
What is the principal muscle that contracts and flattens during inhalation?
Which anatomical structure prevents swallowed food from entering the trachea?
What happens to the thoracic volume when the diaphragm contracts?
options: Increases, lowering pressure to pull air in

mcqs.q: What gas is primarily eliminated from the bloodstream by the respiratory system?

title: Level 06
theoryHtml:
Digestive System breaks down complex ingested food into microscopic nutrients absorbable into circulation. For example : esophagus , stomach, small intestine & colon.

Metabolic Organs produce essential enzymes and digestive fluids. For example : Stomach (Acid churn(Hydrochloric acid and pepsin breakdown proteins)), Small Intestine (Nutrient absorption(Villi absorb glucose, amino acids and lipids)), Liver (Bile synthesis(Secretes bile for fat emulsification and detoxifies drugs)).
notice: Study the theory, go to the task page, answer the questions, complete the level, and open the page for the next level.

mcqs.q: In which organ does the greatest amount of nutrient absorption take place?
What substance is synthesized by the liver to assist in fat digestion?
What acid is produced by parietal cells in the stomach to aid digestion?
What is the primary role of the large intestine (colon)?
options: Water and electrolyte reabsorption and fecal formation

mcqs.q: Which organ stores and concentrates bile until stimulated by food?

title: Level 07
theoryHtml:
Nervous System acts as the master control and communication network, regulating both conscious thoughts and autonomic reflexes. For example : cerebrum , cerebellum, brainstem & spinal nerves.

System Divisions separate executive commands from peripheral senses. For example : Central Nervous System (CNS core(Brain and spinal cord integrate sensory input)), Peripheral Nervous System (PNS relays(Cranial and spinal nerves carry nerve impulses)), Brainstem (Vital autonomic center(Regulates respiration, heart rate and blood pressure)).
notice: Study the theory, go to the task page, answer the questions, complete the level, and open the page for the next level.

mcqs.q: What anatomical structures constitute the Central Nervous System (CNS)?
Which part of the brain controls voluntary movement, reasoning, and higher thinking?
Which brain region is primarily responsible for balance, coordination, and posture?
What vital involuntary functions are controlled by the brainstem?
options: Heart rate, breathing rate, and blood pressure

mcqs.q: What are the specialized functional nerve cells that transmit electrical signals called?

title: Level 08
theoryHtml:
Urinary System maintains fluid balance, regulates blood electrolyte concentrations, and removes nitrogenous waste products. For example : kidneys , ureters, urinary bladder & urethra.

Renal Physiology operates at the microscopic nephron level. For example : Nephron (Functional filtration unit(Glomerulus filters blood plasma into filtrate)), Ureters (Conduit tubes(Propel urine from kidney to bladder via peristalsis)), Urinary Bladder (Storage reservoir(Expandable muscular sac with transitional epithelium)).
notice: Study the theory, go to the task page, answer the questions, complete the level, and open the page for the next level.

mcqs.q: What is the microscopic functional filtration unit of the human kidney?
What tubes transport formed urine from the kidneys to the urinary bladder?
What is the main nitrogenous waste filtered from the blood by kidneys?
Which organ temporarily stores urine until micturition (urination) occurs?
What canal carries urine from the urinary bladder to the outside of the body?

title: Level 09
theoryHtml:
Integumentary System is the body's largest organ system, forming a protective barrier against pathogens, UV radiation, and dehydration. For example : epidermis , dermis, subcutaneous tissue & sebaceous glands.

Cutaneous Layers contribute specialized physiological duties. For example : Epidermis (Avascular shield(Keratinized stratified squamous cells that shed continuously)), Dermis (Vascular support(Contains hair follicles, nerve receptors and collagen)), Sudoriferous Glands (Thermoregulation(Sweat secretion cools body surface)).
notice: Study the theory, go to the task page, answer the questions, complete the level, and open the page for the next level.

mcqs.q: What is the outermost avascular layer of human skin called?
In which skin layer are sensory nerve receptors, hair follicles, and blood vessels located?
What tough, fibrous protein provides strength and water resistance to skin cells?
What pigment produced by melanocytes shields the skin from ultraviolet (UV) radiation?
What is the main physiological purpose of sudoriferous (sweat) glands?
options: Body temperature regulation through evaporative cooling

title: Level 10
theoryHtml:
Endocrine System coordinates slow, long-lasting biological processes by releasing hormones directly into the bloodstream. For example : pituitary , thyroid, adrenal glands & pancreas.

Endocrine Signaling regulates metabolism, growth, and blood chemistry. For example : Pituitary Gland (Master gland(Releases tropic hormones that regulate other endocrine organs)), Pancreatic Islets (Blood glucose control(Secretes insulin and glucagon)), Thyroid Gland (Metabolic rate(T3 and T4 govern cellular caloric consumption)).
notice: Study the theory, go to the task page, answer the questions, complete the level, and open the page for the next level.

mcqs.q: Which endocrine gland is widely recognized as the 'master gland'?
Which hormone is secreted by the pancreas to lower elevated blood glucose levels?
What primary metabolic function is governed by thyroid hormones (T3 and T4)?
options: Basal metabolic rate and energy consumption

mcqs.q: Which glands situated above the kidneys produce epinephrine (adrenaline) and cortisol?
Unlike exocrine glands, where do endocrine glands release their secretions?

title: Level 11
theoryHtml:
Lymphatic System recovers interstitial tissue fluid, returns it to venous blood, and defends against microbial invaders. For example : lymph nodes , spleen, thymus & lymphatic vessels.

Immune Machinery mounts innate and adaptive defenses against pathology. For example : Spleen (Blood filter(Removes aged red blood cells and harbors lymphocytes)), Lymph Nodes (Filtration checkpoint(Clusters of B and T cells that trap pathogens)), Thymus (T-cell maturation(Immunocompetence training center for T-lymphocytes)).
notice: Study the theory, go to the task page, answer the questions, complete the level, and open the page for the next level.

mcqs.q: What is the primary immunological function of lymph nodes?
options: Filter lymph fluid and trap pathogens and foreign particles

mcqs.q: Which lymphatic organ filters blood and destroys worn-out erythrocytes (RBCs)?
Where in the body do T-lymphocytes mature and attain immunocompetence?
What fluid is circulated throughout the lymphatic system?
Which white blood cells are responsible for producing targeted antibodies?

title: Level 12
theoryHtml:
Reproductive System ensures species continuation through gamete production, sex hormone secretion, and fertilization support. For example : ovaries , testes, uterus & fallopian tubes.

Reproductive Organs synthesize sex steroids and nurture embryonic life. For example : Testes (Spermatogenesis(Produce sperm cells and testosterone)), Ovaries (Oogenesis(Release ova and secrete estrogen/progesterone)), Fallopian Tubes (Fertilization site(Normal junction where sperm fertilizes ovum)), Uterus (Gestation chamber(Nurtures fetus throughout gestation)).
notice: Study the theory, go to the task page, answer the questions, complete the level, and open the page for the next level.

mcqs.q: Where does human egg fertilization typically take place?
Which female reproductive organ provides the environment for fetal development during gestation?
What male gonads produce spermatozoa and testosterone?
Which primary female hormones are synthesized by the ovaries?
What is the specialized cellular division that produces haploid gametes called?

title: Level 13
theoryHtml:
Anatomical Terminology standardizes medical documentation so providers communicate without directional ambiguity. For example : sagittal plane , transverse plane, coronal plane & anatomical position.

Directional References establish spatial orientation in medical coding. For example : Anterior / Ventral (Front orientation(Toward the front surface of body)), Posterior / Dorsal (Back orientation(Toward the spine or rear surface)), Proximal vs Distal (Limb reference(Closer to trunk vs farther from point of attachment)), Sagittal plane (Sectional cut(Divides body into right and left halves)).
notice: Study the theory, go to the task page, answer the questions, complete the level, and open the page for the next level.

mcqs.q: Which body plane divides the body into anterior (front) and posterior (back) sections?
What directional term describes a structure closer to the attachment point of a limb?
In standard anatomical position, how are the palms of the hands facing?
Which plane divides the body into superior (upper) and inferior (lower) halves?
What directional term means further away from the midline of the body?

title: Level 14
theoryHtml:
Pathophysiology studies the functional disruptions and cellular changes caused by disease or injury. For example : inflammation , ischemia, necrosis & neoplasia.

Pathological Mechanisms dictate specific diagnostic coding criteria. For example : Acute Inflammation (Cardinal signs(Rubor, calor, tumor, dolor and loss of function)), Ischemia (Hypoxic deficit(Insufficient arterial blood supply causing cellular hypoxia)), Infarction (Tissue necrosis(Localized cell death resulting from severe prolonged ischemia)).
notice: Study the theory, go to the task page, answer the questions, complete the level, and open the page for the next level.

mcqs.q: What are the classic cardinal signs of acute inflammation?
options: Redness, heat, swelling, pain, and loss of function
Nausea, dizziness, and low blood pressure

mcqs.q: What pathological term describes an inadequate blood supply to an organ or tissue?
What is the medical definition of necrosis?
options: Irreversible cellular injury and tissue death

mcqs.q: What does a myocardial infarction (MI) represent in clinical pathophysiology?
options: Death of heart muscle tissue due to prolonged lack of oxygenated blood

mcqs.q: What term describes the spread of cancer cells from an original site to distant organs?

title: Level 15
theoryHtml:
Clinical Coding bridges clinical physiology documentation to standardized ICD-10-CM diagnosis codes for claims, quality metrics, and analytics. For example : etiology , manifestation, laterality & 7th character extensions.

Coding Conventions demand anatomical specificity and documented medical necessity. For example : Laterality (Side specification(Differentiating right limb, left limb, or bilateral)), Excludes1 Notes (Mutually exclusive(Indicates two conditions cannot occur together)), Combination Codes (Unified diagnosis(Single code classifying etiology and secondary manifestation)).
notice: Study the theory, go to the task page, answer the questions, complete the level, and open the page for the next level.

mcqs.q: Why is anatomical laterality (right vs. left) critical in modern ICD-10-CM coding?
options: It specifies the exact anatomical side affected for accurate treatment and billing
It determines the physician's hourly wage
It is only required for dental procedures

mcqs.q: What does an 'Excludes1' instructional note mean in the ICD-10-CM tabular list?
options: The conditions are mutually exclusive and should NOT be billed together
The code requires a 7th character modifier
The code is optional for reimbursement

mcqs.q: What is a combination code in medical coding?
options: A single code used to classify two diagnoses or an etiology and manifestation together
A code used only in emergency rooms

mcqs.q: What does a 7th character extension often indicate in injury and trauma coding?
options: Episode of care (e.g. initial, subsequent, or sequela)

mcqs.q: What principle governs that diagnostic codes must justify procedural codes for payment?
